- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent low, apply a 1–2 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 10–15% for the next 2–3 days.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a downward bias correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast mean.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast deviates > 3% from true, adjust toward historical mean of last 7–10 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid forecasting below 65% of 30-day historical average unless sentiment strongly supports it.  
- If sentiment shows sudden reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33), reduce forecast by 10–15% for next 3–5 days.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true outcome by > 5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply a “mean reversion” rule: subtract 2–5% from next forecast.
